text: And so, the little railway that nobody believed in had forever changed the way people lived, worked and travelled. From a muddy cutting to a nation's lifeline, it stands as a testament to the vision and grit of ordinary men. The rest, as they say, is history.
strengths: the muddy cutting is a concrete starting point
weaknesses: summarises the film instead of ending it
forever changed and a testament to are stock phrases
the final line is the most worn ending in history narration
spokenRhythm: Three sweeping sentences of similar weight, each reaching for a bigger conclusion than the last.
narrativeFunction: Meant to close a film about a railway, but tells the audience what they have just watched.
whyItFails: It answers no question the film asked. It praises instead of reporting, the lifeline is a cliché figure, and the last line is so familiar that it signals a template rather than a writer. Generic history videos end this way, which is the reason the house never does.
rewrite: Hardly anyone had believed in the railway while it was still a muddy cutting. In the end, the country could not do without it.

text: Incredibly, the nugget sold for four hundred dollars — that's well over fifteen thousand dollars in today's money. For a man who had arrived with nothing, it was a heart-pounding, life-changing moment — one he would never forget.
strengths: the sale price is a real figure and a fair place to end
weaknesses: an invented modern conversion presented as fact
tells the listener how the man felt
one he would never forget is a stock closer
spokenRhythm: A sentence split by a dash to carry two figures, then a second dash-split sentence of adjectives.
narrativeFunction: Meant to give the final find its value, but replaces context with a guess and a feeling.
whyItFails: The modern figure is not in any record and cannot be checked, yet it is said as fact. The adverb and the adjectives tell the audience what to feel about a man whose feelings nobody recorded. The real sum, set against a man who had arrived with nothing, is enough.
rewrite: The nugget sold for four hundred dollars, and the man it belonged to had arrived with nothing. The records give no reliable way of saying what that sum was worth at the time.

text: The underwriters paid out in full, and the syndicate quietly dissolved. But one question remains. What really happened aboard the ship that night? Some secrets, it seems, the sea will never give up.
strengths: the payout and the end of the syndicate are clean facts
weaknesses: ends on a tease instead of on what is known
a portentous question the film cannot answer
personifies the sea as a keeper of secrets
spokenRhythm: A plain factual sentence, then three short dramatic lines that each reach for mystery.
narrativeFunction: Meant to leave the audience with the unresolved loss, but turns an honest gap in the record into a cliffhanger.
whyItFails: Not knowing is a fact, and the house says it as one. Dressing it as a question and a secret makes the ending sound like a channel's sign-off and implies there is a hidden answer the film has not found.
rewrite: The underwriters paid in full, and the syndicate was wound up. What happened aboard the ship that night has never been established.

text: It wasn't just a mill. It was a town. It wasn't just a wage. It was a way of life. Looms silent. Gates shut. Workers gone. And the town would never be the same.
strengths: the idea that the mill was the town's livelihood is sound
weaknesses: the same contrast twice in four lines
three fragments as a fake drumroll over the closing shots
a stock closing line about never being the same
spokenRhythm: Eight short sentences in near identical shapes, so the ending has no shape at all.
narrativeFunction: Meant to close a film about a mill town, but recites a formula instead of saying what happened.
whyItFails: The repeated not-this-but-that is the clearest single sign of machine narration. The fragments describe what the closing shots can show. Nothing in it tells the audience a fact they did not already have.
rewrite: The mill had given the town its wages and most of its way of life. When it shut, the workers left, and the town was a different place.

text: In the end, the bank's collapse took the savings of nearly two thousand depositors with it, most of them farmers and shopkeepers who had never set foot in the city. The truth is, this was a story of trust, greed and the stories we tell ourselves about money. A cautionary tale. And perhaps that is the real lesson of everything we have seen.
strengths: the first sentence is a strong, specific ending on its own
weaknesses: moralises after the facts have already landed
the truth is introduces an opinion as if it were a discovery
a cautionary tale and the real lesson are stock closers
spokenRhythm: One good long sentence followed by three lines that each try to sum up the film.
narrativeFunction: Meant to close a film about a bank failure, but explains its own meaning to the audience.
whyItFails: The depositors already tell the audience everything the moral tries to say. A summary of themes, announced as truth and labelled a lesson, is how generic history videos end, and it treats the listener as someone who missed the point.
rewrite: When the bank collapsed, it took the savings of nearly two thousand depositors with it. Most of them were farmers and shopkeepers who had never set foot in the city.
